claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by the interplay between atomic size mismatch and electronic structure.
Atomic size mismatch and electronic structure influence the enthalpy of mixing and entropy contributions to free energy.
The resulting free-energy balance determines whether single-phase or multiphase microstructures form.
The initial homogenized Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Elemental substitutions with larger or smaller atoms can systematically vary atomic size mismatch while retaining an equiatomic composition.
Treatment at 1000°C allows equilibrium phase formation.
Atomic size mismatch alters lattice strain.
Atomic size mismatch alters electronic interactions.
Changes in lattice strain and electronic interactions affect the enthalpy of mixing.
Changes caused by atomic size mismatch affect configurational entropy.
The balance of enthalpic and entropic factors determines whether the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution or decomposes into multiple phases.
Alloys with moderate atomic size mismatch will retain a single-phase solid solution.
Alloys with excessive atomic size mismatch will separate into multiple phases.
Equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni without substitutions is expected to be a single-phase solid solution after the specified treatment.
The hypothesis is limited to equiatomic or near-equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni compositions and may not apply to non-equiatomic compositions or alloys containing additional elements.
The atomic-size-mismatch threshold for phase separation may depend on temperature and processing history.
Formation of a single phase at significant mismatch, or phase separation at minimal mismatch, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes substituting elements to change atomic radii, which may introduce elements outside Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni, while the boundary states that the hypothesis may not apply to alloys with additional elements. No substitutions confined to the stated five-element system are specified.
